subject: genetics
question: **Type:** calculation A dihybrid cross with complete dominance is expected to follow a 9:3:3:1 ratio (sums to 16). Among 160 offspring, how many are expected in the double dominant class?
explanation: The double dominant class occupies 9 parts of the 9:3:3:1 ratio (sums to 16), so the expected count is 9/16 x 160 = 90. B takes one of the 3 part classes, 3/16 x 160 = 30, and C takes the 1 part class, 1/16 x 160 = 10. D applies the single locus probability 3/4 instead of the two locus 9/16, giving 3/4 x 160 = 120.
